subject: Difference in LOD between scanone and fitqtl

messages.author: 6f9e45599f56653d
messages.subject: Difference in LOD between scanone and fitqtl
parts:
Hello, 

I got 2 QTL from scanone search, and got the LOD score (both 3.5) and the position of each QTL using lodint.
Then, with those positions, I performed makeqtl -> fitqtl. It indicated that the LOD scores of those QTL were 2.6. They are not as significant as they were indicated to be by scanone. There was no interaction between the two.

How come scanone and fitqtl give different LOD scores?

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Difference in LOD between scanone and fitqtl
parts:
The LOD scores from scanone compare a model with a single QTL to a model with no QTL.
The LOD scores in your use of fitqtl compare a model with two QTL to a model with one QTL.

So they tend to be different. fitqtl can give LOD scores that are either bigger or smaller; we hope for them to be bigger, but that doesn't always happen.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Difference in LOD between scanone and fitqtl
parts:
Thanks Karl,

With the two QTL, which are not interacted to each other, which is the more accurate way to get the PVE% and effect of each QTL?

1. To perform fitqtl with only one of the QTL at a time?

2. Or can the two QTL be included in one makeqtl-> fitqtl attempt?

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Difference in LOD between scanone and fitqtl
parts:
If you believe there are two QTL, you should study the model that includes both of them.
So yes, use fitqtl with both QTL in the model.

karl
